messages.subject: heterogeneous variograms
parts:
Hi all,

I have a group of 56 elephants that I would like to fit aKDE's to, but I my variograms show remarkable variation in structure (examples below - no periodicity, ~3 weekly, 6 month and annual):

Are there tools to accommodate such structure yet? If not, is the best approach to acknowledge it as a caveat to the home range sizes currently estimated using ctmm.


I dont want to dig to much into the reasons behind this variation just yet, I just want the most robust estimate of home range size currently available to do some basic region/sex comparisons.


Any help much appreciated. 


Best,


Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: heterogeneous variograms
parts:
Hi Chris,

The basic OUF model might fit okay to those, even though it isn't a perfect match (I'm iffy on 3). You should try fitting and compare the empirical variograms and fitted models. The best home-range estimate is more than likely going to be AKDE based on the best trend and autocorrelation model (which we refer to as the "movement model"). You would want to give caveats when your best movement model doesn't seem very good in an absolute sense. But the best movement model will almost never be IID, which is what you assume when doing conventional KDE or MCP.

In some cases of dispersal or migration, you can segment the data to break it up into stationary pieces. This is a stop gap measure until better movement models are developed.

There are periodic models in the package, vignette("periodogram"), but I have not yet coded them to work with akde() as this is very complex.

Best,
Chris
